name: HubSpot
summary: HubSpot hires against its public Culture Code and the HEART traits: Humble, Empathetic, Adaptable, Remarkable and Transparent. It says it hires for culture add rather than culture fit, and uses behavioural questions tied to those traits. For engineers, HubSpot's own prep page says there are no brainteasers: interviewers care about writing and understanding code, working with people and solving real problems, and candidates can look things up during the interview. Candidates commonly report a recruiter screen, a skills assessment and a final round with the team.
rounds: Recruiter screen, often 15 to 30 minutes with some behavioural questions
Skills assessment for some roles, such as a coding exercise or a written task
Final round with the team: for engineers, practical coding and a back-end or front-end session; for other roles, a case or presentation
looks_for: Culture add: a new perspective you bring
Solving real problems with other people

questions.text: Tell me about a time you made someone else look brilliant.
covers: Who it was and what they were working on
What you did to help them shine
What happened for them and the team

questions.text: Tell me about a time you changed your mind after hearing a customer or colleague out.
covers: Your first view
What you heard that changed it
What you did differently

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to adapt quickly when priorities changed.
covers: What changed and why
How you re-planned
What you delivered

questions.text: Tell me about a mistake you made and how you told people about it.
covers: The mistake and its impact
How and when you shared it
What you fixed and learned

questions.text: How would you build a feature that suggests the best time to send a marketing email to each contact?
covers: Signals: past opens and clicks, time zones
A simple first version before a model
How you'd test that it helps

questions.text: A small business customer says the product is too complicated. What do you do?
covers: Finding out what they're trying to do
Quick help now and a product fix later
How you'd tell if it worked

questions.text: Walk me through how you'd model contacts, companies and deals in a CRM database.
covers: Entities and their relationships
Handling duplicates and merges
Queries that must stay fast as data grows

questions.text: How would you grow sign-ups for a free product without hurting how many people stay?
covers: Where people drop off today
Experiments on onboarding and value moments
Measuring retention, not just sign-ups

questions.text: How do you use documentation and search when you're stuck on a coding problem?
covers: Where you look first and why
How you judge what you find
Explaining what you used and why it works

questions.text: Which HEART trait is strongest in you, and which are you working on?
covers: An honest pick for each
An example of each
What you're doing to grow

questions.text: Why do you want to work at HubSpot?
covers: Something specific about HubSpot's customers or culture
How your skills fit the role
What you'd add to the team

questions.text: What perspective would you add to the team that it might not have now?
covers: Your background or experience that's different
How it would help the work
An example of it helping before

tips: Read HubSpot's Culture Code and prepare a story for each HEART trait.
HubSpot says it hires for culture add: be ready to say what new perspective you bring.
For engineering, HubSpot says there are no brainteasers and you can look things up; practise realistic coding with documentation open.
Know HubSpot's product: try the free CRM before your interview.
